about: The mutant ledger of internal/rpcgen's tests, started by Rm (wf10, 2026-11-10): edits of std rpc and its runtime/v1 bodies that only a built rpc server observes. Each mutant names the rule it breaks and the test that kills it, as SUITE:NAME in the shared ledger format.

mutants.name: rpc-answer-buffers
mutants.rule: An ndjson batch is answered as a stream of Exit lines, not as one buffered answer (rpc.md rule 2).

mutants.name: rpc-lines-at-end
mutants.rule: Each Exit line of an ndjson batch is emitted as its call ends, while other calls of the batch are still held.

mutants.name: rpc-mount-exact
mutants.origin: wf10 Rm (R1 rpc-m4, moved into Answer)
mutants.rule: Answer answers the mount with a trailing slash, where Effect's RpcClient (and Call) posts.

mutants.name: rchk-wide-die-defect
mutants.rule: A Die named Unrepresentable (an int the server would not send) is the typed rpc.Unrepresentable for a client (rpc.md, Call and the int rule).

mutants.name: rchk-wide-die-path
mutants.rule: The Die of a refused int carries its path, so the client's Unrepresentable names where the int is.

mutants.name: rchk-lost-defect
mutants.rule: A lost or refused connection and a status other than 200 are rpc.Transport, a typed failure of Call.

mutants.name: rchk-unnamed-defect
mutants.rule: In the checked call, a failure the row does not name is rpc.Transport, not a defect.

mutants.name: rchk-bad-value-defect
mutants.from: return Transport{Reason: "the \(what) is not the contract's: \(text)"}
mutants.rule: A value or failure that is not the contract's fails rpc.Transport in rpc.Decode, so the checked call names it.

mutants.name: rchk-row-no-wide
mutants.rule: The checked row of an operation that carries an int names rpc.Unrepresentable.

mutants.name: rchk-provider-wide-lost
mutants.from: fmt.Fprintf(&b, "case rpc.Unrepresentable as u:\n%srpc.Refuse[%s](u)\n", ret, res)
mutants.to: fmt.Fprintf(&b, "case rpc.Unrepresentable as u:\n%srpc.Lost[%s](rpc.Transport{Reason: u.Path})\n", ret, res)
mutants.rule: The provider raises a refused int as the Unrepresentable defect (rpc.Refuse), as R1 did.

mutants.name: rpcgen-refined-one-step
mutants.rule: The int walker of a defined or refined int converts through its base, int64(int(v)): a refined value converts in one step only to its base.

mutants.name: rpc-method-405
mutants.rule: Another method at the mount is a 404 with no body, as Effect's router (one POST route) answers it.

mutants.name: rpc-malformed-400
mutants.rule: A body that is not Effect RPC's is a 200 whose one message is a Defect, as Effect's server answers it.

mutants.name: rpc-defect-unframed
mutants.rule: The Defect of an ndjson body is an ndjson line, in the body's framing.

mutants.name: rpc-syntax-unnamed
mutants.rule: A body that is not JSON is the Defect named SyntaxError, the error JSON.parse throws in Effect's server.

mutants.name: cli-bool-no-value
mutants.from:
c.print = append(c.print, fmt.Sprintf("out = out.Append(\"-%s=\\(%s)\")", name, acc))
		return convert(kind, conv, f+".Get(v)")
mutants.rule: Print writes a bool flag with its value (-on=false), since a switch alone is true: ArgsRoundTrip.

mutants.name: cli-nested-field-dropped
mutants.from: e := g.leaf(c, f.Type, name, fpath, facc, seen)
mutants.rule: Print writes every field of a nested record: ArgsRoundTrip.

mutants.name: cli-positional-read-as-flag
mutants.rule: Print ends the flags with "--" before the positional arguments, so a negative int or a text that starts with "-" is read as an argument: ArgsRoundTrip.

mutants.name: cli-failure-status-zero
mutants.rule: Run answers a typed failure with status 1, also with --json: the probe's Run tests.

mutants.name: cli-text-is-json
mutants.rule: Run prints a basic value as its text, not its JSON, without --json: the probe's Run tests.

mutants.name: mcp-optional-required
mutants.from:
props = append(props, jsonQuote(key)+":"+g.schema(opt.TArgs[0], seen, where))
			continue
mutants.to:
props = append(props, jsonQuote(key)+":"+g.schema(opt.TArgs[0], seen, where))
			required = append(required, jsonQuote(key))
			continue
mutants.rule: A json.Optional field is not required, since its key can be absent (the plan's mutant; the hub's Schema, which the tools list): ArgumentsFitTheSchema.

mutants.name: mcp-int-as-number-string
mutants.rule: An int field is a JSON integer in the schema: ArgumentsFitTheSchema. The schema is the hub's Schema.

mutants.name: mcp-flat-wrapped
mutants.rule: A tool whose only parameter is a record takes the record's fields as its arguments, and Call wraps them in the parameter's key: ArgumentsRoundTrip.

mutants.name: mcp-failure-untagged
mutants.rule: A typed failure is a ToolError whose message is its tagged JSON, as the rpc package tags it: the probe's Answers tests.

mutants.name: rpc-defined-int-one-step
mutants.rule: A walker converts a type defined over int to int64 through int (S108 refuses one step); the bug: seed 1 of the mcp property drew type Count int.

mutants.name: af0-call-another-reply
mutants.rule: Call answers each operation's value as that operation's Reply: CallIsTheOperation.

mutants.name: af0-failure-other-variant
mutants.rule: Call answers a typed failure in its own type's Failure variant: CallIsTheOperation.

mutants.name: af0-call-swaps-params
mutants.rule: Call passes a Request's fields to the operation in its parameters' order, also two of one type (Pair(key, label)): CallIsTheOperation.

mutants.name: af0-client-failure-defect
mutants.rule: A Client fails a failure of the operation's row as that typed failure, not a defect: ClientIsCall.

mutants.name: af0-same-name-failures-merged
mutants.to: if other, ok := byName[name]; ok && false {
mutants.rule: Two failure types of one name are refused, naming both: their Failure variants and their JSON tags would be one.
